endpoints.description: Service health probe. Reports the resolved state of the two engine modules loaded via dynamic import (media-local, composition-remotion/render), the resolution state of the media binaries (ffmpeg, ffprobe, whisper-cli, the Whisper model, the sherpa-onnx-offline-tts CLI, the TTS voices directory) by logical name and env var — never their resolved host path — and the capabilities enabled in this cycle. Answers 200 in both the ok and degraded states. capabilities gains storyboardQueue in spec-e-burgos-008 cycle-01. The claude CLI is deliberately NOT added to binaries: that list is resolved by @video-maker/media-local and adding it would report degraded on every machine without Claude Code installed, CI included. capabilities gains producerEngines in spec-e-burgos-017 cycle-04.

responses.405: application/json: { error: { code: 'METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED', stage: null, message, resource, expected } } with an Allow header, for any method other than GET on this path.
responses.500: application/json: { error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', stage: null, message } } from the central error handler.

endpoints.description: Creates a job for the project — render (default), montage or storyboard, selected by an optional kind field in the request body. kind absent, an empty body, or a body without a kind field all mean render, byte for byte identical to before this cycle: no request body was ever read for this endpoint prior to spec-e-burgos-007. render: the stored Timeline is read from work/timeline.json, validated and snapshotted once at creation, so a job always renders the Timeline that existed when it was created and never a later PUT. montage: runs ingestProject then autoMontage from @video-maker/auto-montage over media/<slug>/ with preset (default software-demo) and seed (default 0), rejected with 409 if work/timeline.json already exists unless overwrite: true is sent. The job id is generated by the service; for render it is the same id used for out/<id>.mp4 and work/renders/<id>/. Dispatch is FIFO with concurrency 1 across both kinds: the job is born running when the single slot is free and queued otherwise. storyboard: asks the AI agent (the local claude CLI, no API key) for a storyboard and writes work/storyboard.json. It takes exactly one of brief (an idea to turn into a script) or scriptText (an already written script to split into scenes) — neither or both is STORYBOARD_INPUT_INVALID — and is rejected with 409 if work/storyboard.json already exists unless overwrite: true is sent. Its stages are collect (project inventory: catalog assets, A-roll transcript, previous storyboard), propose (the agent call) and persist. spec-e-burgos-014 cycle-01: montage also accepts scriptPath XOR scriptText (the script the voice reads, used to align the captions word by word against it keeping the whisper timings) and logo: 'auto' | 'off' (default auto: if raw/logo/ has an image it becomes the logo layer of the Timeline, bottom-right). Its report gains logoAssetId and scriptAlignment { replaced, removed, inserted, dropped, corrected }. FIX-e-burgos-008-001: storyboard and voice accept an optional model validated against the PRODUCER_MODELS list of the studio producer, so the chat can run a job with the model of the turn; CLAUDE_CLI_MODEL (default sonnet) is the fallback and the agent is never invoked without --model. FIX-e-burgos-007-001: montage accepts format (the OutputPreset of the Timeline, default reels-9x16) and forwards it to autoMontage as outputPreset. FIX-e-burgos-009-001: voice accepts scriptText XOR scriptPath (one sentence per line) as an alternative to the storyboard, plus gapMs (default 900): it synthesizes one wav per sentence, concatenates them with that silence into work/voice/voice.wav (48 kHz mono), transcribes it into work/voice/voice.words.json and writes work/voice/script-manifest.json with source: 'script'. The job report gains source ('storyboard' | 'script'), a nullable storyboardId and a nullable track { path, wordsPath, durationMs, lineCount, gapMs }. FIX-e-burgos-007-002: montage accepts voice: 'aroll' | 'script' (default 'aroll'). With 'script' the speech source is the track the voice job synthesized (work/voice/voice.wav + work/voice/voice.words.json, described by work/voice/script-manifest.json) instead of the A-roll transcript: concepts, B-roll and captions come from those words, the Timeline voice track points at the wav as an audio asset of its own (kind: 'audio', id work/voice/voice.wav), the A-roll audio is ignored altogether, silence pruning is off (a single keep) and the montage lasts min(voice, A-roll). The report gains voiceSource and a nullable voiceTrack { assetId, durationMs, truncatedMs }. FIX-e-burgos-009-002: kind 'voice' accepts timestamped script lines — [m:ss], [mm:ss] or [m:ss-m:ss] (range separator -, – or —) — mixed freely with unmarked lines. With marks each sentence is placed at its own start (one adelay per segment plus a non-normalizing amix) instead of being chained, and work/voice/script-manifest.json gains four optional per-line fields always written by the pipeline: endMs, requestedStartMs (null without a mark), overflowMs and lengthScale. A sentence that does not fit its window first loses the gapMs cushion, then is re-synthesized with Piper --length-scale down to 0.85 (a 15% limit), and only then displaces the next line, which is recorded as startMs !== requestedStartMs plus overflowMs > 0. schemaVersion stays at 1 and a script with no mark behaves exactly as before. kind 'montage' with voice: 'script' lasts the WHOLE A-roll when the manifest is timed (the narration ends earlier, the tail stays silent, truncatedMs is 0 and the Timeline voice clip is clipped to the wav duration) and keeps min(voice, A-roll) with truncatedMs otherwise. FIX-e-burgos-003-003: kind 'montage' accepts captionStyle — 'bold-impact' | 'clean-sans' | 'outline-pop' | 'subtle-lower' | 'off' — written into timeline.captionStyle and read by the Remotion composition to choose the typographic preset ('off' renders no captions). Absent, the montage preset decides: educational → 'subtle-lower', software-demo/hardware/recipe → 'bold-impact' (the behaviour before the fix). 'subtle-lower' also switches the word grouping to a subtitle (6–10 words per caption over 2–4 s in the lower box). The montage report gains captionStyle, always resolved. When the last timed line declares a range end the track is padded with silence up to it (apad=whole_dur), and a montage over a timed track reports voiceTrack.truncatedMs against the end of the last sentence, never against that padding. A timed script passed to the montage as scriptPath/scriptText is stripped of its marks before the caption alignment, so the brackets never reach a caption.

request_body.schema: { kind?: 'render' | 'montage' | 'storyboard' | 'voice' | 'photo-aroll', preset?: string, seed?: number, overwrite?: boolean, scriptPath?: string, scriptText?: string, logo?: 'auto' | 'off', brief?: string, voice?: string, sceneIds?: string[], gapMs?: number, model?: string, format?: 'reels-9x16' | 'tiktok-9x16' | 'shorts-9x16' | 'youtube-16x9', captionStyle?: 'bold-impact' | 'clean-sans' | 'outline-pop' | 'subtle-lower' | 'off', photos?: string[], output?: string, fps?: 30 } — every field optional; preset/seed/scriptPath/scriptText/logo are read only when kind is 'montage', brief/scriptText only when kind is 'storyboard', sceneIds/gapMs only when kind is 'voice' (and scriptText/scriptPath are read by 'voice' too, as the alternative to the storyboard), overwrite by montage, storyboard and voice, format only when kind is 'montage', and model by storyboard and voice (validated against PRODUCER_MODELS; storyboard passes it to the CLI as --model, voice accepts it for uniformity and ignores it). voice is overloaded by kind: on a 'voice' job it is a voice-model id from GET /voices, on a 'montage' job it is the speech source, 'aroll' (default) or 'script'. captionStyle is read only when kind is 'montage'. photos (required, non-empty array of project-relative paths, each resolved through the producer path resolver and required to sit under raw/images/), output (required, a single portable file name; the target is raw/aroll/<output>) and fps (optional, must be exactly 30 when present, the only supported frame rate) are read only when kind is 'photo-aroll'.

responses.202: application/json: the full Job — { id, kind, slug, state, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt, progress, report, error } — with a location: /jobs/<id> header. 202 and not 201: the job resource exists and is queryable immediately, the deliverable does not.

No job is registered and no file is touched. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }. No job is registered. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID for a slug that is not a single kebab-case path segment; JOB_KIND_INVALID when kind is present and neither 'render' nor 'montage'; (kind: render only) TIMELINE_INVALID when the stored document does not parse or validate; (kind: montage only) MONTAGE_PRESET_INVALID, MONTAGE_SEED_INVALID, MONTAGE_OVERWRITE_INVALID for an invalid parameter, or MONTAGE_RAW_MISSING (surfaced when the async job settles, not at request time) when raw/ has no role directory. No job is registered for any of the request-time codes. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }. STORYBOARD_INPUT_INVALID (kind: storyboard) when brief and scriptText are both absent, both present, or not a non-empty string; STORYBOARD_OVERWRITE_INVALID when overwrite is not a boolean; JOB_KIND_INVALID now names 'render', 'montage', 'storyboard', 'voice' or 'photo-aroll'. No job is registered. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }. MONTAGE_SCRIPT_INVALID (kind: montage) when scriptPath and scriptText are both present or either is not a non-empty string; MONTAGE_LOGO_INVALID when logo is neither 'auto' nor 'off'. No job is registered for either. JOB_MODEL_INVALID (kind: storyboard or voice) when model is present and is not one of PRODUCER_MODELS; no job is registered. MONTAGE_FORMAT_INVALID (kind: montage) when format is present and is not one of the four output presets; no job is registered. spec-e-burgos-017 cycle-01 (TASK-004): fifth job kind 'photo-aroll' builds the Product ad A-roll from photos with no agent-side ffmpeg. Reads work/voice/script-manifest.json (written by a prior kind: 'voice' job with a script) and builds one Ken Burns clip per manifest line — duration from that line's startMs to the next line's startMs, the last line to the manifest's total durationMs, so every cut lands on a photo change and the total equals the narration; photos cycle when there are fewer than lines and only the first N are used in the given order when there are more. Frames are computed as round(seconds × fps) and used identically as zoompan's d= and ffmpeg's -frames:v, never -t. Clips are concatenated (concat demuxer, -c copy) and the narration (work/voice/voice.wav) is muxed in with the existing EP-006-style mux port. Intermediates live under work/producer/ad/. responses.200: application/json: { slug: string, jobs: [{ id, kind, state, stage, errorCode, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt }] }. A slug with no jobs answers an empty jobs array, whether or not the project exists.

endpoints.description: Full detail of a single job (render, montage, storyboard, voice or photo-aroll) in any of its six states (queued, running, canceling, succeeded, failed, canceled). changelog.change: Adds a kind: 'render' | 'montage' field. A job still queued, running or canceling when the service restarts is marked failed with error.code JOB_INTERRUPTED at startup, before the server accepts requests. endpoints.description: Requests cancellation of a job (render or montage). Cancellation is real but cooperative: no process is ever signalled or killed. A queued job is canceled immediately without invoking a single pipeline port. A running job moves to the observable transitional state canceling and settles as canceled at the next stage checkpoint (for montage: only before ingestProject starts or before autoMontage starts — never mid-way through either opaque call), after the binary in flight finishes its current invocation. A job canceled while its last stage is in flight still settles as canceled with report: null even though its on-disk artifacts (out/<jobId>.mp4 for render; work/catalog.json for montage) may already exist and be complete — the entry state wins over the pipeline result. Nothing on disk is ever deleted.

responses.200: application/json: the full Job with state: 'canceled', for a job that was queued. Terminal and done.
responses.202: application/json: the full Job with state: 'canceling', for a job that was running — accepted, still in flight. Repeating the request on an already canceling job answers 202 again, idempotently, and is never a 409.
responses.404: RENDER_JOB_NOT_FOUND for an id the queue does not know. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.409: RENDER_JOB_NOT_CANCELABLE for a job already in a terminal state (succeeded, failed or canceled). Its final state is never changed. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.500: application/json: { error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', stage: null, message } } from the central error handler.

The route is not project-scoped: voices belong to the machine, not to a project.

request_body.schema: Takes no request body.

endpoints.description: Attaches a locution the user recorded to one scene of the storyboard. The file must already be under raw/voice/ (uploaded with EP-006 and the voice role); this endpoint only names it. A later voice job never replaces an uploaded track, which is how RF-7 is enforced: the recorded locution wins over the synthesized one. The call is synchronous and runs ffmpeg and whisper-cli inline, so a long take holds the connection: turning it into a fourth job kind is a decision left to a future cycle.

endpoints.description: Sends one user message to the producer and starts a turn. The turn runs OUTSIDE the job queue (D-1 of the cycle): the agent enqueues montage/render jobs on this same API and waits for them, so a turn sitting in a queue of concurrency 1 would deadlock itself. Exclusion is per project: one running turn per slug. The user message is persisted before the 202 answers, so the chat can render it immediately. Cancellation kills the child process (it is not the cooperative cancellation of the job queue). The model of the turn is chosen per message: model is optional and validated against PRODUCER_MODELS; when it is absent the service keeps the model of the session and falls back to PRODUCER_MODEL. The model in effect is persisted in session.json, and switching model on a later turn is supported (claude -p --resume <id> --model <m>). Since spec-e-burgos-017 cycle-04 (TASK-004), the engine is resolved per turn from the producer settings (GET/PUT /settings/producer, resolveEffectiveProducerEngine): claude-cli spawns the CLI as before; openrouter runs the turn in process via libs/producer-tools' OpenRouter runtime, rebuilding history from the stored conversation instead of a resumed CLI session (D-C4-05), and never persists session.json for that engine. The OpenRouter API key is read from the macOS keychain (EP-039); it is missing → 409 OPENROUTER_KEY_MISSING, checked before the turn is reserved.

Any other field is ignored.

endpoints.description: Cancels a running producer turn by killing its child process (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace period). endpoints.description: Searches Wikimedia Commons (generator=search over the File namespace, filetype:audio, formatversion=2) for the producer's search_free_music MCP tool, replacing the old curl-to-Commons shell trick. Calls only https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php with a descriptive User-Agent. Keeps only results whose mime is one of audio/mpeg, audio/wav, audio/x-wav, audio/vnd.wave, audio/flac, audio/x-flac, audio/ogg, audio/opus or application/ogg (Commons reports .ogg/.opus/.oga containers as application/ogg) and whose extmetadata LicenseShortName is CC0, Public domain/PDM, CC BY or CC BY-SA (any version) — CC BY-NC, CC BY-ND and files with no LicenseShortName are dropped. durationMs is required by the contract, so a result with no numeric imageinfo.duration is dropped rather than reported as null. Artist is HTML-stripped into author. resultId is a stable non-cryptographic hash of the File: title. Results are cached in memory per project slug for 1 hour (runtime.musicSearchCache) so EP-035 can resolve a resultId; a fresh search replaces the previous cache entry for that slug. Network failure, a non-200 status or unparseable JSON all become MUSIC_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE — the Commons response body is never included in the error.

endpoints.description: Downloads a music result found by EP-034 for the producer's import_music MCP tool. resultId must come from this project's search cache (EP-034), not expired (1h TTL) — otherwise MUSIC_RESULT_UNKNOWN. Downloads only if the file's own url host is exactly upload.wikimedia.org (defense in depth on top of the fact the url was already produced server-side by EP-034), requires a content-length header to enforce the 50 MB cap up front (a response with no content-length is refused rather than streamed unbounded), and writes through the existing upload-temp-then-promote flow (work/.uploads, same as asset upload) into raw/audio/<file name>, where <file name> is the last path segment of the Commons download url; if that name is already taken it is suffixed -2, -3, ... before the source is ever touched, so an import never overwrites an existing file. The whole read-cache/download/promote/write-credit sequence is serialized per project on the same uploadSerializer as asset upload/copy. Appends one entry to work/credits.json (created if missing, existing entries kept; a corrupt existing file is treated as empty rather than blocking the import).

endpoints.description: Retries a job that is failed or canceled by creating a brand new job (a fresh id, retry_of set to the original) with the same kind and the same kind-specific parameters the original job was created with — for kind 'render', the exact Timeline snapshot the original job rendered, never a live re-read of work/timeline.json. Creation reuses the same handler code POST /projects/:slug/jobs runs, so a retry is validated by the exact same preconditions a fresh request of that kind would be (e.g. a montage retry still checks TIMELINE_ALREADY_EXISTS; overwrite is not carried over from the original request, so a retry always behaves like overwrite: false). The original job's own record is never modified: its state, report and error stay exactly as they were.

endpoints.description: Searches Wikimedia Commons (generator=search, filetype:video or filetype:bitmap) and the NASA Image and Video Library (images-api.nasa.gov/search) for the producer's search_free_media MCP tool. Commons: video keeps mp4/webm directly; an ogv result is kept only if a transcoded webm derivative exists (prop=videoinfo&viprop=derivatives), otherwise dropped; image keeps jpg/png/webp. Both kinds require a free commercial extmetadata LicenseShortName (CC0, Public domain/PDM, CC BY, CC BY-SA). NASA: an item is kept only when it has neither photographer nor secondary_creator, or when that credit text contains 'NASA' (drops third-party credits like 'Rocket Lab'); the asset URL is read from the item's collection.json, preferring <id>~medium.mp4 (video) or <id>~large.jpg falling back to <id>~orig.<ext> (image); manifest URLs are upgraded from http to https before use. NASA license is always the fixed string 'NASA (public domain, NASA media usage guidelines)'. Both sources are queried in parallel and merged (Commons first); either one failing does not fail the search as long as the other answers, but both failing raises MEDIA_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. Results are cached in memory per project slug for 1 hour (runtime.freeMediaSearchCache) so EP-047 can resolve a resultId; a fresh search replaces the previous cache entry for that slug.

request_body.schema: Takes no request body.

responses.200: application/json: { results: [{ resultId, source: 'commons'|'nasa', kind: 'video'|'image', title, license, author, pageUrl, durationMs, width, height }] }, at most maxResults entries. Shape frozen as producer-tools STUDIO_TOOLS.search_free_media.output — downloadUrl is kept server-side only and never leaves this response.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.422: INVALID_INPUT when query is missing/blank, kind is not 'video'/'image', or maxResults is missing or outside 1..10; PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.503: MEDIA_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE when neither Wikimedia Commons nor the NASA Image and Video Library answers with a usable response. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.

endpoints.description: Downloads a free media result found by EP-046 for the producer's import_media MCP tool. resultId must come from this project's search cache (EP-046), not expired (1h TTL) — otherwise MEDIA_RESULT_UNKNOWN. Downloads only if the file's own url host is exactly upload.wikimedia.org or images-assets.nasa.gov, requires a content-length header to enforce the size cap up front (200 MB video, 30 MB image; a response with no content-length is refused rather than streamed unbounded), and writes through the existing upload-temp-then-promote flow (work/.uploads) into raw/broll/<file name> (video) or raw/images/<file name> (image); if that name is already taken it is suffixed -2, -3, ... before the source is ever touched. The whole read-cache/download/promote/write-credit sequence is serialized per project on the same uploadSerializer as asset upload/copy and music import. Appends one entry to work/credits.json (kind 'video' or 'image', next to existing 'music' entries; created if missing, existing entries kept; a corrupt existing file is treated as empty rather than blocking the import).

endpoints.description: Downsizes 1 to 6 project image paths with ffmpeg to a JPEG at most 1280px on the long side under work/frames/previews/, so the producer agent's view_images MCP tool can read the bytes back through GET /projects/:slug/files/*path and show the model the photo, the same delivery pattern extract_frames uses for video. Uses a dedicated resizeImage port (libs/media-local ffmpeg/resize-image.ts), not extractFrame: an image2 input's near-zero reported duration makes ffmpeg's -ss seek past its only frame and write nothing, even at -ss 0, so resizeImage omits -ss entirely (-i path -frames:v 1 -vf scale -q:v). The preview file name is a deterministic hash of the source path (deps.hashText), so re-previewing the same photo reuses the same file. view_images has no outputSchema in the MCP server (Claude Code CLI 2.1.123 forwards structuredContent instead of image blocks when one is declared), and the OpenRouter runtime returns the images as file parts only when the active model accepts images.

responses.200: application/json: { previews: [{ path, previewPath }] }, one entry per input path in order. Shape frozen as producer-tools STUDIO_TOOLS.view_images.output.

responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, or FILE_NOT_FOUND when a source path is not a file in the project. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.422: INVALID_INPUT when paths is missing or not an array of 1 to 6 non-empty strings; PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
responses.500: MEDIA_COMMAND_FAILED, MEDIA_OUTPUT_UNPARSEABLE or MEDIA_BINARY_NOT_FOUND (503) when ffmpeg fails on one of the paths, translated by translateEngineError. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint? } }.
